title: What do you guys use for AI art generation?
author: Revolutionary_Lie85
selftext: Im completely new to game development, i tried a little bit before AI and understand a bit what it's about but I can't code at all so I'm using ai sadly, i started on my first project and its a 2D pixel game but as a solo dev with no resources and no talent on art creation i want to use AI to make the art for me, any idea what i could be using to make this dream come true?

comments.author: morfidon
comments.body: I just generate directly through codex

replies.author: Fizassist1
replies.body: this has been the most reliable for consistent assets for me.. although I burnt through my weekly limit in a day lol  also use ludo ai, and pixellab

comments.author: yungastronot
comments.body:
90+% of people here use Chatgpt Image 2.0. I can tell because theres a certain look to it that you can never unsee once you notice. There's a way to prompt it to not have that look but it takes a detailed prompt and certain art styles.

I found Grok Imagine to be better until they recently updated the model. So I use a combination of the two + photoshop to achieve an less obvious AI look.

comments.body: Adobe Firefly. It only sources art owned by Adobe and the results are commercially safe to use and no artists are ripped off.

comments.author: ZymzAlchemy
comments.body:
Each model will take the exact same prompt and produce a different outcome. 

My workflow is to take pencil sketches and feed them into the chat box with a prompt for styling and context. I have found for 2D sprites a simple pencil sketch given to ChatGPT produces some good results. This also works with Gemini / Lumo etc. Most of those offer free tiers you can use to test the output and pick the one you like most. 

Best advice here, don't spend money on AI tools you don't need, for something like this there's plenty of free services. IDK what agent you're using for code, but if you're using ChatGPT/Codex already, then you have what you need at your fingertips. 

Good luck, and keep creating.

comments.author: Entropydemic
comments.body:
I'm kinda in the same boat as you. I use SpellAi to generate a basic image (you get like 150 free images per hour), then I give the image I like to Gemini to translate into video. Gemini itself recommends Claude for everything game dev, so after my time expires I'll try that. Gemini says it's also cheaper than most other game dev models and you can "talk to it like a companion" so we'll see.

Anyway I use a very generic prompt to get the video cell I like, cut it into gifs, then take the cells of the given gif into a sprite sheet. THEN I use GiMP (free) to cut away the keyframe color and then Aseprite ((most valuable 20 bucks you'll spend on a sprite tool, but there is a free version you can recompile also)) to animate it.

https://i.redd.it/ada814t86yjh1.gif

replies.author: Varrianda
replies.body: I’ll be honest though, 100% AI art just isn’t good enough to rely on. If you’re not an artist it’ll be painfully obvious. For prototyping it’s fine, but for a finished product you’ll get a lot of hate.
